ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the side length of square $ABCD$ is $4$, and point $E$ is a point inside the square. Connect $BE$ and $CE$, and $\angle ABE = \angle BCE$. Point $F$ is a moving point on side $AB$, connecting $FD$ and $FE$. What is the minimum value of the length of $FD+FE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ABE + \angle CBE = 90^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle ABE = \angle BCE$, \\
$\therefore \angle BCE + \angle CBE = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BEC = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ point E moves on the semicircle with BC as the diameter, \\
As shown in the diagram, let the midpoint of BC be O, and construct the square APGB symmetric to square ABCD with respect to line AB, then the corresponding point of D is P, \\
Connect PO, intersecting AB at F and the semicircle O at E, then the length of segment EP is the minimum value of $FD+FE$, OE $= 4$, \\
Since $\angle G = 90^\circ$, PG $=$ BG $=$ AB $= 4$, \\
$\therefore$ OG $= 6$, \\
$\therefore$ OP $= \sqrt{PG^2 + OG^2} = \sqrt{4^2 + 6^2} = 2\sqrt{13}$, \\
$\therefore$ EP $= 2\sqrt{13} - 2$, \\
$\therefore$ The minimum value of the length of FD+FE is $\boxed{2\sqrt{13} - 2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there is a square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point F is on the left side AB, point E is inside the square, and BE, CE, FE, and FD are drawn. Then reason: the side length of the square is 4, so ∠ABC=90°. Because E is inside, ray BE divides ∠ABC into ∠ABE and ∠CBE, therefore ∠ABE+∠CBE=90°. Also it is known that ∠ABE=∠BCE, so ∠BCE+∠CBE=90°. In triangle BCE, it can be obtained that ∠BEC=90°, therefore E lies on the semicircle with BC as diameter. BC=4, so the center O of this semicircle is the midpoint of BC, and the radius is 2. Use the unfolding method: reflect D about line AB to point P. Because F is on the axis of symmetry AB, FD=FP. Therefore FD+FE=FP+FE. By the triangle inequality, FP+FE≥PE, and equality holds when P, F, E are collinear. So the problem is transformed into finding the minimum distance from point P to point E on this semicircle. Take coordinates B=(0,0), C=(4,0), A=(0,4), D=(4,4). Reflecting D about AB, namely x=0, gives P=(-4,4). O=(2,0). Thus OP=sqrt((2-(-4))^2+(0-4)^2)=sqrt(6^2+4^2)=2sqrt(13). The nearest point from point P to the semicircle is at the intersection of PO and the semicircle, and the minimum PE=OP-radius=2sqrt(13)-2. Also line PO intersects AB at a point on AB, so the corresponding F can be taken, and equality can be realized.

method.method_draft: Geometric unfolding route. First read the diagram as a square ABCD with A top-left, B bottom-left, C bottom-right, D top-right, F on side AB, and E inside connected to B, C, F, while FD is also drawn. From the text use side length AB=BC=CD=DA=4 and angle ABE = angle BCE. Since angle ABC=90°, angle ABE + angle CBE=90°; substituting angle ABE=angle BCE gives angle CBE + angle BCE=90°, so angle BEC=90°. Hence E lies on the upper semicircle with diameter BC, center O the midpoint of BC and radius 2. Reflect D across line AB to a point P outside the square on the left; because F lies on the mirror line AB, FD=FP. Thus FD+FE=FP+FE. For any choice of F and E, FP+FE is at least PE, with equality when P,F,E are collinear. Therefore minimize PE over E on the semicircle. The closest point of the semicircle to P lies on line PO; this line crosses segment AB, so the equality path is feasible. Compute with coordinates B=(0,0), C=(4,0), D=(4,4), so P=(-4,4), O=(2,0). Then OP=sqrt(6^2+4^2)=2sqrt(13), and the minimum PE is OP-2=2sqrt(13)-2.

method.method_draft: Coordinate optimization route. Read the diagram with B at the lower-left corner, A above it, C to the right of B, D above C, F on AB, and E inside. Set coordinates B=(0,0), A=(0,4), C=(4,0), D=(4,4). Let F=(0,t), where 0<=t<=4, and E=(x,y). From angle ABE = angle BCE, use tangents: tan(angle ABE)=x/y and tan(angle BCE)=y/(4-x), so x/y=y/(4-x). Hence y^2=x(4-x), equivalently (x-2)^2+y^2=4; E lies on the upper semicircle centered at O=(2,0) with radius 2. For fixed F, the smallest possible FE over this semicircle is the distance from F to the circle, namely FO-2=sqrt(t^2+4)-2, with the nearest point lying on the upper semicircle. Also FD=sqrt(4^2+(4-t)^2). Thus minimize phi(t)=sqrt(16+(4-t)^2)+sqrt(t^2+4)-2 on [0,4]. Differentiate: phi'(t)=(t-4)/sqrt(16+(4-t)^2)+t/sqrt(t^2+4). raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the side length of square $ABCD$ is $4$, and point $E$ is a point inside the square. Connect $BE$ and $CE$, with $\angle ABE = \angle BCE$. Point $F$ is a moving point on side $AB$. Connect $FD$ and $FE$. What is the minimum value of $FD+FE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ABE + \angle CBE = 90^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle ABE = \angle BCE$, \\
$\therefore \angle BCE + \angle CBE = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BEC = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ point $E$ moves on the semicircle with $BC$ as the diameter. \\
As shown in the diagram, let the midpoint of $BC$ be $O$, and construct the square $APGB$ symmetric to square $ABCD$ with respect to line $AB$, then the corresponding point of $D$ is $P$. \\
Connect $PO$, intersecting $AB$ at $F$ and the semicircle at $E$, then the length of segment $EP$ is the minimum value of $FD+FE$, $OE = 4$. \\
Since $\angle G = 90^\circ$, $PG = BG = AB = 4$, \\
$\therefore OG = 6$, \\
$\therefore OP = \sqrt{PG^2 + OG^2} = \sqrt{4^2 + 6^2} = 2\sqrt{13}$, \\
$\therefore EP = 2\sqrt{13} - 2$, \\
$\therefore$ the minimum value of the length of $FD+FE$ is $\boxed{2\sqrt{13} - 2}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: in the figure there is a square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point F is on the left side AB, point E is inside the square, and BE, CE, FE, and FD are drawn.
Then reason: the side length of the square is 4, so ∠ABC=90°. Because E is inside, ray BE divides ∠ABC into ∠ABE and ∠CBE, therefore ∠ABE+∠CBE=90°. Also it is known that ∠ABE=∠BCE, so ∠BCE+∠CBE=90°. In triangle BCE, it can be obtained that ∠BEC=90°, therefore E lies on the semicircle with BC as diameter. BC=4, so the center O of this semicircle is the midpoint of BC, and the radius is 2.
Use the unfolding method: reflect D about line AB to point P. Because F is on the axis of symmetry AB, FD=FP. Therefore FD+FE=FP+FE. By the triangle inequality, FP+FE≥PE, and equality holds when P, F, E are collinear. So the problem is transformed into finding the minimum distance from point P to point E on this semicircle.
Take coordinates B=(0,0), C=(4,0), A=(0,4), D=(4,4). Reflecting D about AB, namely x=0, gives P=(-4,4). O=(2,0). Thus OP=sqrt((2-(-4))^2+(0-4)^2)=sqrt(6^2+4^2)=2sqrt(13). The nearest point from point P to the semicircle is at the intersection of PO and the semicircle, and the minimum PE=OP-radius=2sqrt(13)-2. Also line PO intersects AB at a point on AB, so the corresponding F can be taken, and equality can be realized.
